items.headline: Haaland remains captain as FPL managers weigh up the Jackson bandwagon
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the preferred captain for Gameweek 9 despite Manchester City facing Brighton, with his record against the Seagulls — returns in six of seven meetings, including an assist in the one match he does not score — outweighing Brighton boss Fabian Hürzeler’s unbeaten league record against City. Cole Palmer is the leading alternative at home to Manchester United after serving his suspension in the League Cup, but Haaland is the clear first choice. Nicolas Jackson is a viable differential captain against Fulham, although the recommendation is not to chase that route over Haaland.

Jackson is the dominant transfer of the week after his brace against Manchester City and multiple price rises, with effective ownership expected to become a major rank risk. However, buying him is not automatic for teams with more urgent issues. The preferred move is Malick Thiaw to Bournemouth’s Silva, rather than João Pedro to Jackson, because Thiaw has been benched and could remain a longer-term minutes problem. Silva is viewed as close to a season keeper thanks to Bournemouth’s extended fixture run, while João Pedro’s absence is treated as temporary and Gross can autosub in this week.

Jackson remains an attractive option after the international break, when Aston Villa’s run includes Sunderland at home, Ipswich away, Everton at home and Crystal Palace at home. Unai Emery indicates that Jackson and Manzambi should be available for Fulham despite missing training, but Jackson’s immediate appeal has to be balanced against Villa’s busy schedule, possible European rotation and the opportunity cost of tying up funds in attack. Cheaper forwards such as Thierno Barry, Evanilson and Dominic Calvert-Lewin offer routes to preserve money for Arsenal defender Gabriel, who is considered a major long-term target once Arsenal’s fixtures improve and Aston Villa’s Konsa eventually loses his place to William Saliba.

Barry is narrowly preferred over Evanilson and Calvert-Lewin as the cheaper forward option: he ranks second in the league behind Haaland for expected goal involvement and expected goals, and follows a goal and assist against Newcastle in the League Cup with Newcastle away and Coventry at home next. Evanilson is also in form and has the better immediate fixture case, while Calvert-Lewin is a plausible João Pedro replacement around Gameweek 10 or 12. The broader strategy is to avoid unnecessary hits, retain flexibility through the international break and not make a knowingly inferior transfer simply to match Jackson’s ownership.

For selection calls, Silva, Van Hecke and Mendy are favoured over Konsa, with Mendy expected to return after training and offering strong defensive-contribution potential against Ipswich. Konsa is only marginally ahead of Riccardo Calafiori, whose attacking upside is offset by fitness and minutes uncertainty away to Liverpool. City leaks suggest Foden and Cherki are benched while Haaland, Doku, Dias and Gvardiol start, but the information carries a warning: Manchester City are reportedly aware of early leaks and could alter plans to expose the source.
key_points: Captain Haaland over Palmer and Jackson for Gameweek 9, with Palmer the strongest alternative against Manchester United.
Sell Malick Thiaw for Bournemouth’s Silva rather than forcing João Pedro to Jackson, especially with only one free transfer.
Jackson is a major ownership threat but can still be bought after the break for Villa’s strong Gameweek 11-15 fixture run.
Keep João Pedro where possible this week, allow Gross to autosub, and reassess a switch to Calvert-Lewin or another forward later.
Barry is the preferred budget striker over Evanilson and Calvert-Lewin because of elite underlying numbers, low price and upcoming Newcastle and Coventry fixtures.
Mendy is expected to start against Ipswich after positive training comments; start him ahead of Konsa or De Cuyper in close bench decisions.
Avoid hits for marginal defender upgrades or to remove playable assets, with several Gameweek 9 defensive calls too close to justify a minus four.
Treat reports of Foden and Cherki being benched cautiously, despite leaks naming Haaland, Doku, Dias and Gvardiol as starters.

items.headline: Silva replaces Thomas as Haaland remains the clear Gameweek 9 captain
items.summary:
The key transfer is Thomas to Silva, strengthening a defence built around players with defensive-contribution potential, reliable minutes, solid clean-sheet prospects and some attacking threat. Silva is preferred as a long-term Bournemouth option over more expensive defenders such as Gabriel, while Van Hecke is also endorsed for managers prioritising the immediate fixture. The view is that FPL managers have little value in premium attackers at present, so spending budget on a playable bench and dependable defenders is a valid strategy.

The starting decision is Gross over Sharda. Gross offers penalties, set pieces and dependable 90-minute potential, whereas Sharda carries greater upside but comes with concerns over form, fitness and minutes after an early substitution in Gameweek 8. Sharda is not an urgent sale because the squad can cover him, but he is a likely future exit around Gameweek 11 unless his role improves. Barry ranks highly among forward options and starts ahead of Gross, while Jackson is the preferred Joao Pedro replacement despite unsubstantiated pre-deadline concern over his absence from some training pictures.

Haaland is the overwhelming captain choice for Gameweek 9, with Palmer the vice-captain. Palmer has a strong fixture against Manchester United and remains far too good to bench, but Haaland is considered the safer armband choice. Rogers and Jackson are acceptable differential captain alternatives, while Tavanier captaincy is viewed as unnecessarily ambitious against a Leeds side with a strong defensive record.

A Free Hit is rejected because two free transfers solve the squad’s immediate problems. Gameweek 12, when Arsenal play Manchester City, remains a possible Free Hit window, but it is not yet compelling enough to commit. For managers already using the chip in Gameweek 9, the preferred structure includes Haaland, Palmer, Rogers, Jackson, Barry, Pedro Porro, Van Hecke, Silva and Tavanier, with Ryan a viable short-term alternative to Tavanier. A reported Manchester City leak suggests Foden and Cherki are benched while Gvardiol starts, so Cherki owners are advised to use the information cautiously but plan as though he may not start.
key_points: Transfer Thomas to Silva, with Silva viewed as a rapidly emerging long-term Bournemouth defensive pick.
Start Gross over Sharda because Gross has penalties, set pieces and stronger minute security; Sharda remains benchable rather than an urgent sale.
Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9 and vice-captain Palmer; Palmer is a strong play against Manchester United but not the preferred armband.
Jackson is the leading Joao Pedro replacement, ahead of Barry, Calvert-Lewin and Evanilson; missing training photos do not constitute reliable injury news.
Avoid defender hits in Gameweek 9, with managers encouraged to start available options such as Calafiori, Thomas or De Cuyper instead.
Reported Manchester City team news has Foden and Cherki on the bench and Gvardiol starting, although leaks are never certain.
Do not use the Free Hit merely to solve short-term injuries when transfers can cover them; Gameweek 12 remains under consideration but is not confirmed.
Van Hecke is preferred for immediate fixture appeal, while Silva is preferred as the more reliable every-week defensive hold.

items.headline: Jackson Transfer Carries Late Fitness Risk as Haaland Remains the GW9 Captain
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 arrives with Erling Haaland as the clear captaincy choice, despite a difficult-looking slate of fixtures and widespread uncertainty over team news. Cole Palmer takes the vice-captaincy rather than new signing Nicolas Jackson, while Chelsea’s attacking outlook looks far less convincing without the injured Joao Pedro. Palmer and Morgan Gibbs-White are both under pressure after disappointing runs, but neither is sold immediately because the available replacements and fixtures do not make a compelling short-term case.

The main transfer is Gonzalo Garcia to Jackson, but late concerns emerge after Jackson is absent from Aston Villa training pictures and Villa’s win odds shorten. Unai Emery’s comments do not confirm an injury, so Jackson remains in the squad, but managers yet to buy him are advised to avoid the risk and consider Evanilson instead. Evanilson is not viewed as a standout one-week pick against Leeds, yet Bournemouth’s upcoming fixture run makes him an attractive medium-term forward. Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Alexander Isak are also viable alternatives, with Isak offering stronger long-term upside if the budget does not damage the rest of the squad.

Joao Pedro is ruled out for a few weeks but is held with only one free transfer, as he is expected to have a chance of returning after the international break and would likely need buying back. The alternative considered is a -8 to sell Gibbs-White for Bournemouth midfielder Antoine Semenyo or Tavernier/Ryan and upgrade Slater to Manzambi. That move would improve depth and cover Pedro’s absence, but it is rejected because it depends on a hit paying off immediately, while Calafiori’s return to Arsenal training means Slater does not have to start. A hit may become more appealing in Gameweek 10 if Palmer or Gibbs-White continue to underperform and the extra money can be redistributed into Bournemouth assets.

Bournemouth midfielders are the priority attacking targets for the coming weeks. Tavernier is the safer, more rounded selection because of his chance creation and bonus-point potential, while Ryan is a high-upside differential with exceptional recent shot volume, although poor finishing and limited bonus potential make him riskier. Manzambi has appeal as a cheap enabler but carries minutes concerns. In defence, Calafiori is preferred to Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa if Arsenal’s training update is trusted, while Lewis Hall and Egan are strong starts. Double Arsenal defence is acceptable, but a triple-up is considered excessive against Liverpool; Djed Spence/Diker-type defenders facing Manchester City are generally benchable unless squad injuries force them in.

A Free Hit is considered but held back, as the best one-week selections — Bournemouth, Aston Villa and Spurs defensive assets — are also players managers want to own beyond Gameweek 9. Gameweek 15 is earmarked as a more plausible Free Hit window because Bournemouth visit Arsenal, Chelsea face Manchester City and Leeds travel to Liverpool. The immediate aim is to survive Gameweek 9 without further hits, then use the international break and Bournemouth’s Gameweek 10 trip to Ipswich to rebuild squad depth and restore flexibility.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9, with Palmer preferred as vice-captain over Jackson because of late Aston Villa fitness concerns.
Gonzalo Garcia is sold for Nicolas Jackson, but managers who have not moved yet should favour Evanilson if they want to avoid Jackson’s possible injury risk.
Joao Pedro is held despite being out for a few weeks because he may return after the international break and there is only one free transfer available.
A proposed -8 involving Gibbs-White to a Bournemouth midfielder and Slater to Manzambi is rejected, although a restructuring hit in Gameweek 10 remains possible.
Tavernier is the safer Bournemouth midfield pick for creativity and bonus, while Ryan is the higher-risk differential because of his elite shot volume.
Calafiori trains with Arsenal and is preferred to Konsa if starting security is trusted, but avoid a triple Arsenal defensive stack against Liverpool.
Evanilson is the preferred forward alternative to Jackson and is a strong medium-term buy ahead of Bournemouth’s favourable run.
Gameweek 15 is the early Free Hit target, with Bournemouth at Arsenal, Chelsea against Manchester City and Leeds at Liverpool.

items.headline: Haaland remains the Gameweek 9 captain as Jackson fitness doubts cloud Villa transfer plans
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout Gameweek 9 captain despite Brighton’s strong form. Manchester City still carry the league’s most potent attack and Haaland remains the highest-upside option, while alternatives such as Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Antoine Semenyo lack either the fixture, form or certainty to justify a major captaincy gamble. A differential captain is better saved for a week in which Haaland has a genuinely difficult fixture and another premium has a clear favourable matchup.

Nicholas Jackson remains a high-upside replacement for Joao Pedro, but the move carries late uncertainty. Unai Emery says Jackson and Amadou Onana/Manzambi missed the Bournemouth cup tie for “different reasons, not only rest” and should normally play Fulham, yet Jackson is absent from selected training images and Aston Villa’s projected-goal markets shorten amid the speculation. The expectation remains that Jackson starts against Fulham, but managers selling a fit starter may reasonably avoid the risk. If Jackson is already owned, he is worth holding; if confirmed absent, upgrading a cheap midfielder such as Sangare to Marcus Tavernier is preferable to panicking into another striker move.

Defence produces the major selection dilemma. Riccardo Calafiori trains after his recent flag and has greater attacking upside than Ezri Konsa, but there is a meaningful risk of reduced minutes or a substitute appearance against Liverpool. Konsa is the safer pick because he is certain to start, can collect defensive-contribution points and offers set-piece threat. Calafiori is the upside play if managers accept the risk; Konsa is the sensible choice for those protecting a score. Arsenal defenders are not automatic starts away to Liverpool, even with decent clean-sheet odds, and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall, Bournemouth options such as Marcos Senesi/James Hill, and Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke are viable alternatives depending on budget and fixture horizon.

Most teams are best served by rolling transfers rather than chasing marginal upgrades. Tavernier is an attractive medium-term buy, but moving a playable midfielder such as Morgan Gibbs-White, Harvey Barnes or Pascal Gross solely to fund him is not essential. Gross is usually the expendable bench option in crowded midfields because Manchester City away is difficult, although his penalties and secure minutes keep him viable. Evanilson is preferred to Dominic Calvert-Lewin when a forward must start regularly over the next few weeks, while Calvert-Lewin is useful if his tougher fixtures can be benched. Reports that Phil Foden and Rayan Cherki are benched increase the appeal of City wingers Jeremy Doku and Oscar Bobb/Savio only as short-term punts, not as reliable long-term picks.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9; Brighton are capable opponents, but City’s attack and Haaland’s ceiling still outweigh the available alternatives.
Jackson is expected to start against Fulham but carries enough late fitness and rotation uncertainty that new buyers should assess their bench strength before moving from Joao Pedro.
Hold Jackson if already owned rather than selling on speculation; if he is definitively ruled out, a Sangare-to-Tavernier type upgrade is a logical contingency.
Start Calafiori only if willing to accept a minutes risk against Liverpool; Konsa is the safer selection through guaranteed starts, defensive-contribution potential and set-piece threat.
Avoid using a free hit primarily to remove Arsenal defenders for Liverpool away unless the wider squad has multiple serious problems.
Tavernier is a good longer-term target, but managers with playable midfields can roll and reassess after the international break.
Evanilson is the stronger forward for sustained starts across the next few gameweeks, while Calvert-Lewin works better as a fixture-dependent rotation option.
Treat reports of Foden and Cherki being benched as a reason to avoid them this week; Doku is a viable short-term differential but remains a Manchester City minutes risk.

items.title: JOÃO PEDRO OUT ❌ | FPL GW9 INJURY + TEAM NEWS 🚨|  FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Joao Pedro absence forces Gameweek 9 transfer rethink as Grealish faces Everton punishment
items.summary:
Joao Pedro is the standout FPL concern ahead of Gameweek 9 after being ruled out for at least several weeks, with Gameweek 11 the earliest plausible return and no firm timetable from Chelsea. He is also expected to miss the international break, so managers can sell with confidence if they need an immediate replacement, although prospective wildcards can wait for further clarity. Cole Palmer is available again after serving his one-match ban in midweek, while Moises Caicedo is fit; Reece James, Enzo Fernandez and others remain sidelined.

Arsenal offer potential boosts for the visit to Liverpool, with Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard all back in training and potentially available if they complete final sessions. Noni Madueke faces a late fitness test, but Bukayo Saka and William Saliba remain absent until after the international break. Jurrien Timber begins a three-match suspension after Arsenal's unsuccessful appeal. Liverpool may welcome back Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz, while Florian Wirtz has already returned from an ankle issue; Bradley, Frimpong and Leoni remain out.

At the budget end, Brentford's Yehor Yarmolyuk remains suspended, strengthening Ibrahim Sangare's prospects of another start alongside Vitaly Janelt, who returns from a ban. Nottingham Forest's Neco Williams is fit despite an elbow problem, while Nicolas Dominguez and Dan Ndoye require checks but could return. Bournemouth's Marcus Tavernier has no significant issue after being withdrawn in midweek, and Evanilson's cup absence is confirmed as a rest. Kroupi is not yet ready to start, while Leeds' Anton Stach remains a doubt with a foot injury.

Everton's team news carries the biggest selection risk beyond Pedro: Jack Grealish misses the midweek match for a club-discipline breach and David Moyes declines to confirm whether he will return against Newcastle. Managers should prepare for the possibility of another absence. Jarrad Branthwaite is expected to clear concussion protocol and be available on Monday, while Iliman Ndiaye is back after playing 86 minutes in midweek. Newcastle's Joelinton is also a major doubt after twisting an ankle, which could improve Will Osula's chance of a start if the Brazilian cannot recover.

Elsewhere, Brighton regain Yankuba Minteh and Mats Wieffer, with Ferdi Kadioglu and Andreas expected to be options against Manchester City. Spurs have James Maddison and Destiny Udogie available again, although Rodrigo Bentancur serves the final match of his suspension. Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta is rested rather than injured, but Ismaila Sarr remains out. Hull's Nuno Tavares is back in training but may not start, while Sunderland's Wilson Isidor is expected to return to the squad.
key_points: Sell Joao Pedro if an immediate transfer is needed: he is out for at least a few weeks and Gameweek 11 is only the earliest possible return.
Cole Palmer is available after his midweek suspension, while Arsenal's Calafiori, Rice and Odegaard could return for Gameweek 9.
Jack Grealish is a major selection doubt after Everton omit him for a disciplinary breach, with no confirmation that he returns against Newcastle.
Ibrahim Sangare has a strong chance of starting for Brentford because Yehor Yarmolyuk remains suspended, despite Vitaly Janelt returning from his own ban.
Neco Williams is fit for Nottingham Forest, while Nicolas Dominguez and Dan Ndoye need late assessments ahead of Brentford.
Jarrad Branthwaite is expected to be available for Everton after concussion protocol, and Joelinton is doubtful for Newcastle with an ankle injury.
Jean-Philippe Mateta is merely rested in midweek and should be available for Crystal Palace, but Ismaila Sarr remains out.
Kroupi is not ready to start for Bournemouth, while Leeds midfielder Anton Stach remains a doubt with a foot problem.

items.title: FPL GW9 Team Selection: Two Transfers Used! 🚨 | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Antonio Silva joins Haaland and Jackson as Gameweek 9’s long-term FPL building blocks
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 presents an unusually flat fixture landscape, particularly for clean sheets, so there is little value in overreacting to difficult defensive match-ups. Tottenham have the best clean-sheet odds against Crystal Palace, but most sides—including Arsenal away to Liverpool—sit close together around the 30% mark. Arsenal’s defensive quality keeps them viable despite the fixture, while Leeds defender Maremovic remains playable for his defensive-contribution floor. Bobby Thomas is a late fitness call after a calf issue, but is considered worth starting if fit because he is more likely to start or miss out entirely than make a damaging one-point cameo.

The midfield is led by Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers at home to a struggling Manchester United, with Chelsea expected to create chances against a side short on confidence. Bryan Mbeumo remains a hold despite blanking against Bournemouth: with Sesko out for months, he continues centrally and could take penalties if Bruno Fernandes is absent. Sharda is given one more chance against Nottingham Forest after a poor, early-substituted display last week, but he is under pressure and could soon be replaced by a cheaper option such as Manzambi. Gross is benched, while Calafiori is first substitute ahead of Dipper after returning to Arsenal training; Dipper is avoided against Manchester City because Brighton’s clean-sheet prospects are poor and his underlying attacking numbers outside Gameweek 1 are modest.

Joao Pedro’s injury forces the first transfer, with Aston Villa’s Jackson arriving after being rested in midweek. Jackson is in form, ranks highly for recent shots and shots in the box, and has a strong fixture run from Fulham in Gameweek 9 through to Chelsea in Gameweek 16, including Manchester United, Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry. The second transfer is Thomas to Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva, a long-term defensive target who combines frequent defensive contributions, major set-piece threat and a Bournemouth side ranked third for expected goals conceded. Silva’s schedule is exceptionally strong, with Arsenal away in Gameweek 15 and Brighton away in Gameweek 20 the only obvious benches before Gameweek 31.

Erling Haaland is the straightforward captain and Palmer the vice-captain. The strategy is to use both free transfers rather than deploy the Free Hit, building a deeper, more flexible squad while premium assets outside Haaland fail to justify their cost. A Gameweek 12 Free Hit remains under consideration because the existing squad could contain triple Arsenal defence against Manchester City, Haaland away to Arsenal and several other awkward fixtures; alternatively, future free transfers can reduce Arsenal exposure and bring in options such as Vuskovic, Manzambi or a Bournemouth attacker.
key_points: Use both free transfers rather than Free Hit in Gameweek 9: Joao Pedro to Jackson and Bobby Thomas to Antonio Silva.
Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9, with Palmer as vice-captain.
Jackson is backed for form, shot volume and Aston Villa’s favourable Gameweek 9-16 run.
Antonio Silva is the priority defensive buy because he offers defensive contributions, set-piece goal threat, bonus potential and Bournemouth’s elite underlying defensive numbers.
Keep Mbeumo despite his recent blank, as Sesko’s long-term absence should preserve his central role and potential penalty duty.
Start Sharda over Gross for Nottingham Forest, but treat Sharda as a short-term audition after his poor Gameweek 8 display.
Do not force defensive transfers for a single Gameweek: clean-sheet odds are tightly grouped, and Arsenal remain competitive even away to Liverpool.
Consider a Gameweek 12 Free Hit if triple Arsenal defence versus Manchester City and Haaland away to Arsenal cannot be comfortably managed with transfers.

items.title: FPL GW9 COMPLETE GUIDE ⁉️ CALAFIORI AVAILABLE ✅ J.PEDRO INJURED ❌ | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Jackson edges Evanilson as João Pedro absence reshapes Gameweek 9 transfer plans
items.summary:
João Pedro is expected to miss Chelsea’s matches against Manchester United and Sunderland and may not return until after the international break, with Leeds at home in Gameweek 10 a possible but uncertain comeback. Managers with several saved transfers are advised to sell, particularly with Jackson, Evanilson and Calvert-Lewin offering attractive replacements; those with only one free transfer should consider how easily they could buy João Pedro back. His absence also weakens the appeal of Chelsea attackers: Cole Palmer is a hold for Manchester United at home rather than a buy, while Rogers remains a reasonable long-term hold or purchase despite Chelsea’s poor league scoring record without João Pedro.

Jackson is the preferred forward buy for Gameweek 9, narrowly ahead of Bournemouth’s Evanilson. Both have stronger immediate upside than Calvert-Lewin, whose next five fixtures are difficult and whose away open-play output is poor, although Calvert-Lewin is the safer set-and-forget option. Isak is also viable for managers upgrading from João Pedro, but his price and Arsenal fixture make the cheaper in-form options more appealing. The preferred attacking combination is Jackson plus a Bournemouth midfielder, with Jackson, Tavernier and Ryan the ideal trio if budget allows; Evanilson and Manzambi save money but are rated slightly below that combination, partly because of Manzambi’s early substitutions.

Tavernier is the safest Bournemouth midfield purchase, thanks to his proven FPL record and good positions, though his recent returns have benefited from defensive errors and he has only 0.5 xG across his last four matches. Ryan is the higher-risk differential, with 12 penalty-box shots in that period compared with Tavernier’s three, while Manzambi is a cheaper alternative with appealing Fulham-at-home fixture but less secure minutes. Pascal Gross remains buyable despite Manchester City, due to set pieces, penalties and dependable game time; Dewsbury-Hall is a lower-owned midfield option for Everton’s improving fixtures. Managers are urged not to overload on Bournemouth, however, as Leeds are capable of taking a result.

Arsenal’s Calafiori, Rice and Saliba train ahead of Liverpool away, although Calafiori’s start is not guaranteed after his Gameweek 8 benching. Gabriel is increasingly attractive at around £8m, especially as Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Saka underperform and free funds for premium defenders, but buying an Arsenal defender before Liverpool is not essential. In goal, Kinsky is the preferred Gameweek 9 play, while Raya is a strong long-term option but ranks unusually low for this week because an Arsenal clean sheet at Anfield is not expected. Erling Haaland is the overwhelming captaincy choice, with Manchester City projected as the highest-scoring side and Haaland leading for goal, assist and predicted points.
key_points: Sell João Pedro if you have transfer flexibility, but retain him only if a quick return for Leeds in Gameweek 10 is worth preserving in your structure.
Do not buy Cole Palmer while João Pedro is injured; hold him for Manchester United at home rather than making a rushed sale.
Jackson is the top forward transfer, Evanilson is second, and the preferred double-up is Jackson with Tavernier or Ryan from Bournemouth.
Tavernier is the safe Bournemouth midfielder, while Ryan is the more explosive differential and Manzambi is the cheaper but less secure-minutes option.
Calvert-Lewin is a hold and a stable long-term pick, but Jackson and Evanilson have greater short-term upside.
Calafiori trains ahead of Liverpool, but Gabriel is the more secure Arsenal defensive investment if managers can afford the premium price.
Avoid starting Raya or relying heavily on Arsenal defensive returns at Liverpool if you have stronger alternatives, with Spurs defenders favoured against Crystal Palace.
Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9; Jackson, Palmer, Tavernier and Bruno Fernandes are only differential vice-captaincy considerations.

items.title: 🚨 Calafiori update 🚨 FPL GW9 Final Thoughts 🤔
items.headline: Nicholas Jackson edges Evanilson as Andy banks transfers ahead of Gameweek 9
items.summary:
Nicholas Jackson is the preferred replacement for the injured João Pedro ahead of Gameweek 9, with Andy already making that move in his own squad. Jackson is favoured over Bournemouth’s Evanilson because he is more trusted as a proven scorer and should retain strong minutes for Aston Villa, although Evanilson is a credible cheaper alternative for managers who need the £0.5m saving. Alexander Isak is judged the superior long-term forward, with Liverpool’s fixtures improving markedly from Gameweek 10, but his £9.1m price and the two-transfer restructuring required make him less appealing for teams not already set up to buy him.

Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9, while Manchester City teammate Rayan Cherki is worth holding despite the usual rotation concern. Cherki appears first choice at No.10 and Phil Foden also playing 90 minutes in midweek slightly strengthens the case for Cherki to start against Brighton. Bryan Mbeumo remains a hold rather than a buy: he should benefit from Sesko’s absence until January, but Chelsea away in Gameweek 9 and Liverpool away in Gameweek 11 are not ideal entry points. Phil Foden is an excellent start only for managers confident he starts; otherwise his minutes risk makes him a bench candidate.

The major defensive call concerns Arsenal’s Riccardo Calafiori. He has returned to training and is likely to start against Liverpool, but carries a residual risk of a bench cameo after his yellow flag. Andy is therefore less keen to sell him, particularly with Hull at home in Gameweek 10, though starting the guaranteed Arsenal defender Kiwior instead is understandable. For new defensive purchases, Bournemouth’s Silva narrowly beats Spurs’ Van Hecke as an every-week option because of Bournemouth’s defensive level and Silva’s stronger defensive-contribution potential; Van Hecke is attractive for managers targeting his favourable home fixtures or rotating with another defender.

In midfield, Tavernier is narrowly preferred to Aston Villa’s Manzambi because his output and role are more established, but Manzambi offers a cheaper, lower-owned route into Villa’s attack. Liverpool’s Gakpo is a watchlist differential from Gameweek 10 thanks to a £7.1m price, improved minutes and a long favourable fixture run, though competition across Liverpool’s front line limits his security. Andy’s own likely Gameweek 9 plan is to captain Haaland, start Calafiori alongside Raya despite the Liverpool fixture, play Lewis Hall and Van Hecke, and roll his remaining two free transfers rather than upgrade Sangare to Tavernier before the international break.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 9, with Manchester City at home to Brighton.
João Pedro is out for weeks, and Nicholas Jackson is the preferred one-transfer replacement; Evanilson is a viable cheaper alternative.
Alexander Isak is a strong differential and arguably the best long-term forward from Gameweek 10, but buying him may require costly squad restructuring.
Riccardo Calafiori trains and is likely to face Liverpool, but owners must accept a small risk that he is benched or makes a cameo.
Rayan Cherki is worth holding for Brighton at home, while Phil Foden should only start if his place in the XI is trusted.
Tavernier is the safer midfield buy over Manzambi, while Manzambi is the cheaper, lower-owned upside pick.
Bournemouth’s Silva is marginally preferred to Spurs’ Van Hecke for a regular defensive slot because of defensive contributions and team form.
Andy plans to roll two remaining free transfers after buying Jackson, prioritising flexibility through the international break.

items.title: FPL GW9 EXPERTS TEAM 🚀 62x Top 1k! 🚨 BEST TEAM!
items.headline: Haaland dominates Gameweek 9 captaincy as João Pedro owners pile into Jackson
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 is a busy one for elite FPL managers, with only 2% of the 273-manager sample rolling a transfer. The defining move is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson: 86% of João Pedro owners sell him and 82% of buyers bring in Jackson, attracted by his fixtures, recent form and a straightforward route back to João Pedro if the injured forward returns in Gameweek 11. Not every manager follows the move, however. Evanilson/Barry and Dominic Calvert-Lewin offer cheaper alternatives, while holding João Pedro is a calculated gamble for those who can field a viable XI and want to avoid buying him back immediately after the international break.

Haaland is the overwhelming captaincy choice, backed by 95% of the experts for Manchester City’s match against Brighton. His record against Brighton is compelling: he has returned in all seven career meetings, with seven goals and one assist, even if City have often found the fixture difficult. Cole Palmer is the distant alternative captain, while isolated managers back Harvey Barnes, Jackson or Morgan Gibbs-White for a differential. The recommended expert XI features Raya; Thomas, Konsa and Mee; Palmer, Rogers, Schär and Tavernier; plus Haaland, Jackson and Calvert-Lewin, with Thomas worth starting despite being a major doubt because many bench alternatives have poor fixtures.

The broader theme is a weakening, shifting template. João Pedro’s injury, concerns around Calafiori, and divisions over premium midfielders have created more variation than in recent weeks. Marcus Tavernier is the leading midfield buy after 45 minutes in the League Cup, while Bournemouth’s run of 14 goals scored and none conceded across their last five matches strengthens interest in him and defensive options. Thiago Silva at £5.0m and Jan Paul van Hecke at £4.9m are highlighted as strong longer-term defensive value, with Silva preferred marginally for his favourable run. Alexander Isak also attracts longer-term buyers despite facing Arsenal next, having scored six goals in seven games.

A wildcard squad illustrates the desired reset: retain Haaland, Palmer and Bryan Mbeumo for secure minutes and upside; add Gabriel as the standout premium defender; and use Jackson alongside Calvert-Lewin rather than maintain heavy Chelsea coverage. Palmer survives despite underwhelming recent returns because of penalties, set pieces and reliable minutes. Managers with multiple problems are encouraged to consider structural fixes rather than repeatedly spending transfers on injuries and flags, while those with playable squads are advised not to overreact to one difficult gameweek. Banking transfers where possible remains valuable ahead of the international break and a potential move towards more defence-heavy structures.
key_points: Nicolas Jackson is the clear Gameweek 9 transfer target, with most João Pedro owners making the direct switch after Pedro’s injury.
Erling Haaland is captained by 95% of the expert sample for Brighton away, supported by returns in all seven of his career matches against them.
Marcus Tavernier is the leading midfield buy, with Bournemouth in excellent form after scoring 14 and conceding none in their past five matches in all competitions.
Thiago Silva and Jan Paul van Hecke are promoted as value defensive additions, with Silva viewed as the stronger long-term hold at £5.0m.
João Pedro can be held only if a manager has a strong alternative XI and wants to be positioned for a possible Gameweek 11 return, but it carries the risk of missing Jackson’s favourable run.
Gabriel remains the preferred premium defensive pick, while a broader move towards a back four is under consideration as defensive value improves.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Barry are viable cheaper alternatives to Jackson, with Calvert-Lewin’s minutes and penalties providing his appeal.
Avoid taking unnecessary hits or forcing short-term fixture moves when highly owned assets such as Groß and Calafiori also have difficult fixtures.

items.title: JOAO PEDRO OUT! 🚩 | Josh's FPL GW9 Team Selection
items.headline: Haaland captains a Jackson-led Gameweek 19 squad after João Pedro exit
items.summary:
With the free transfer already used, the key Gameweek 19 move is João Pedro out for Nicolas Jackson. Jackson faces Fulham at home and arrives in strong form, making him the preferred Chelsea attacking option despite concern that Chelsea are less potent without João Pedro. Erling Haaland partners Jackson up front and holds the captaincy armband.

Kinski starts in goal after a nine-point clean sheet against Chelsea and now hosts Crystal Palace. The defence is Gabriel, Lewis Hall and Jan Paul van Hecke: Gabriel remains an expensive but high-upside pick after his 17-point haul, Hall is retained for Everton after Newcastle’s improved display against Crystal Palace, and Van Hecke is backed against a Palace attack viewed as one of the league’s weakest.

The midfield consists of Morgan Gibbs-White, Harvey Barnes, Pascal Gross, Morgan Rogers and Kevin Schade. Gibbs-White is kept despite frustrating returns, while Barnes starts after scoring against Palace. Gross remains a hold even with Manchester City away, Rogers is trusted to find returns against Manchester United, and Schade gets another chance against Nottingham Forest despite being substituted early last week.

Leno, Timothy Castagne, Riccardo Calafiori and De Cuyper make up the bench. Castagne is an uncomfortable omission given Manchester City’s defensive vulnerability, but there is no clear starter to bench in his place. With no free transfer remaining, the squad relies on the existing defensive match-ups, Jackson’s form and Haaland’s captaincy upside.
key_points: João Pedro is transferred out for Nicolas Jackson, who hosts Fulham in Gameweek 19 and is selected on the strength of his recent form.
Erling Haaland is captain for Gameweek 19, with Jackson joining him in the starting forward line.
Kinski starts in goal against Crystal Palace after returning nine points and a clean sheet versus Chelsea.
Gabriel, Lewis Hall and Van Hecke start in defence, with Hall facing Everton and Van Hecke facing a low-scoring Palace side.
Pascal Gross is held and started despite an away fixture against Manchester City.
Morgan Rogers is backed against Manchester United, while Kevin Schade starts against Nottingham Forest despite his early substitution last week.
Castagne is benched despite the appeal of facing a leaky Manchester City defence, because there is no obvious player to replace in the XI.

items.title: My FPL GW9 Free Hit Team! 💥 #fpl
items.headline: Haaland is the standout Free Hit captain for Gameweek 9 as Spurs defence anchors the draft
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captaincy pick in a provisional Free Hit squad for Gameweek 9, with Manchester City hosting Brighton. The forward offers the safest combination of ceiling and reliability in the one-week team, while the draft also includes Thiago as a short-term punt against Nottingham Forest. Thiago has produced an attacking return in four straight matches, takes penalties and is expected to play 90 minutes; he is not viewed as strong long-term value, but his home fixture makes him attractive for a Free Hit. Nicolas Jackson is the other forward named, with Fulham the opposition.

Caoimhin Kelleher starts in goal for the home match against Nottingham Forest, identified as the league's weakest attack. Forest's poor finishing is seen as helpful not only for clean-sheet potential but also for save points. The defence doubles on Tottenham, with Pedro Porro and Jan Paul van Hecke selected for Crystal Palace at home. Spurs have the best clean-sheet odds of the gameweek, and while their attack has disappointed as an FPL source, their underlying defensive numbers remain encouraging. Porro adds set-piece involvement and attacking upside, while Van Hecke and Antonio Silva are picked partly for defensive-contribution potential; Silva faces Leeds at home.

Chelsea's home game against Manchester United drives a midfield double-up on Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, with United considered vulnerable under their unchanged manager. Manzambi is included for Fulham because of his strong attacking volume, while Tavernier earns a place on current form. The draft is built around favourable home fixtures, clean-sheet probability and one-week upside rather than long-term price value.

The Free Hit is not confirmed, however. Its use depends on late injury news in the existing squad, so the proposed XI is a strong Gameweek 9 template rather than a locked-in final team.
key_points: Captain Haaland at home to Brighton in Gameweek 9.
Start Kelleher against Nottingham Forest, whose weak attack could provide both clean-sheet and save-point potential.
Double up on Spurs defenders Porro and Van Hecke for Crystal Palace at home, the gameweek's leading clean-sheet fixture.
Porro is preferred for his set pieces and attacking threat, while Van Hecke and Antonio Silva offer defensive-contribution routes to points.
Back Palmer and Rogers against Manchester United, with Chelsea expected to exploit United's defensive weakness.
Thiago is a one-week Free Hit punt against Nottingham Forest after four consecutive attacking returns, with penalties and likely 90 minutes strengthening the case.
Delay activating the Free Hit until injury news clarifies whether the existing squad requires the chip.

items.title: My Team Selection for Gameweek 9 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 9 captain as Jackson replaces injured João Pedro
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the straightforward captain for Gameweek 9, with Manchester City hosting Southampton. The goalkeeper situation is less appealing, with David Raya facing Liverpool, but a goalkeeper transfer is not considered worthwhile this week.

The defence is built around Jan Paul van Hecke, who has both a favourable Wolves fixture and some attacking upside, plus Lewis Hall at home to Everton. Hall is not a priority buy and could be sold in the near future, but he is a good enough starter for this round. Gabriel forms an Arsenal defensive double-up with Riccardo Calafiori, although Calafiori is benched while yellow-flagged. If Calafiori is ruled out beyond the international break, he is likely to be sold for Manchester City’s Bernardo Silva, with Ezri Konsa dropping to the bench; if he has a chance of returning for Gameweek 10, he is worth holding.

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers stay despite Chelsea’s poor display against Liverpool and João Pedro’s injury. Their upcoming schedules remain favourable enough to justify patience. Evanilson also keeps his place after blanking on his debut in the squad: with Enes Ünal ruled out until January, the Bournemouth forward should receive regular minutes as the central striker. Bryan Mbeumo has a difficult trip to Manchester City in Gameweek 9, but Brentford’s fixtures improve markedly from Gameweek 10, so he is retained.

The early transfer is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson, completed before the price changes. João Pedro is expected to miss at least the period before the international break, while Jackson offers a more secure short-term route into Chelsea’s attack and benefits from their good fixtures.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland against Southampton in Gameweek 9.
Transfer João Pedro out for Nicolas Jackson after João Pedro’s injury is expected to keep him out until at least the international break.
Start Jan Paul van Hecke for Brighton’s home match against Wolves, with his set-piece and goal threat adding appeal.
Lewis Hall starts against Everton but remains a potential future sale rather than a player to buy now.
Hold Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers because their fixture runs remain strong despite recent underwhelming returns.
Keep Evanilson as Bournemouth’s likely first-choice No. 9 while Enes Ünal is out until January.
Monitor Riccardo Calafiori’s fitness: sell him for Bernardo Silva if his absence extends beyond the international break, but hold if he can return for Gameweek 10.
Retain Bryan Mbeumo through Manchester City away because Brentford’s fixtures improve from Gameweek 10.

items.title: WILDCARD ACTIVE?! | AZ's FPL GW9 Team Selection
items.headline: Palmer makes way as Haaland, Isak and Gabriel anchor a Gameweek 9 Wildcard
items.summary:
A Gameweek 9 Wildcard is under serious consideration after a difficult round featuring injuries and Cole Palmer’s red card. The existing squad has too many concerns: Riccardo Calafiori carries a flag and may face reduced minutes during a congested spell, Palmer has underperformed for much of the season, Morgan Gibbs-White has lacked end product, João Pedro is injured, and Thomas may be absent for an extended period. The proposed reset also moves away from Mbeumo despite his returns, with Manchester United still not trusted as an attacking proposition.

The defensive core is built around a Kinsky-Trafford goalkeeper rotation, which is viewed as particularly favourable because of the upcoming home fixtures. Leif Davis, Mohamovic and Gabriel form the main defence, with Gabriel preferred to Calafiori despite the higher price because of his security and attacking potential. Mohamovic is also backed as a regular starter alongside Uskovic, except in prohibitive fixtures such as Arsenal or Manchester City.

The midfield sacrifices Palmer for Morgan Rogers, Antoine Semenyo, Marcus Tavernier and Rodon, with Tavernier selected after a strong start to the campaign. Groves is temporarily benched for the Manchester City away fixture but is expected to return to the side in Gameweek 10. Up front, the Wildcard keeps premium firepower through Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak, while Nicolas Jackson supplies form and depth; Consor is retained as a bench option.

The appeal of the structure is that it avoids an expensive midfield premium and creates a strong 15-man squad, with multiple playable options and likely price rises. The downside is persistent benching dilemmas and inevitable bench points, particularly with Bench Boost no longer available. There is concern about selling Palmer before Manchester United because of his penalty potential, but Chelsea’s poor form and João Pedro’s injury reduce confidence that Palmer’s output will improve immediately.
key_points: A Gameweek 9 Wildcard is favoured after injuries, Palmer’s red card and several underperforming players leave the current squad needing a reset.
Gabriel is preferred to flagged Calafiori because Calafiori’s minutes may be less secure during the Champions League and Christmas schedule.
Kinsky and Trafford are selected as a rotating goalkeeper pair on the strength of their upcoming home-fixture rotation.
Palmer is sold for Morgan Rogers, with Chelsea’s poor form and João Pedro’s injury judged to outweigh Palmer’s penalty appeal against Manchester United.
Haaland, Isak and Jackson form the attacking core, giving the squad two elite captaincy options plus Jackson’s current form.
Tavernier is a midfield differential after his strong start, while Groves is only benched for the Manchester City away match before returning in Gameweek 10.
The no-premium-midfield structure creates a deep squad but brings weekly selection problems and the risk of significant bench points.

items.title: FPL GW9 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 9 Team Plans
items.headline: João Pedro exit fuels Nicolas Jackson rush as Haaland dominates Gameweek 9 captaincy
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 is a clear action week for Fantasy Premier League managers, with 47% of surveyed experts making one transfer, 28% making two and 17% making three or more. Only 2% roll a transfer, while around 7% deploy a Wildcard or Free Hit. The high activity reflects a combination of injuries, squad clean-up and attractive fixture runs, particularly for Aston Villa and Bournemouth assets.

João Pedro is the standout sell after news that he is expected to miss at least two gameweeks. Eighty per cent of the experts who own him move him on, making João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson the overwhelmingly preferred transfer. Jackson is viewed as a long-term pick rather than a one-week punt: Aston Villa have an extended favourable run, he is rested in midweek and begins with Fulham at home in Gameweek 9. Gonzalo to Jackson and Wissa to Jackson are also strongly backed routes into the Villa forward.

If a second striker transfer is needed, experts are more willing to consider Alexander Isak or Evanilson, although Jackson is markedly preferred as the primary replacement. Isak offers upside but is a less comfortable immediate buy because of Arsenal, while Evanilson is generally treated as a secondary forward move rather than the direct João Pedro successor. In midfield, Tavernier is a leading buy ahead of Leeds at home, with Saka, Sangaré and Cherki among the suggested sales. Manzambi is the cheaper alternative for managers unable to afford Tavernier.

Defensively, Silva is the most popular incoming defender, with Gabriel, Van Hecke and Hill also attracting interest. Calafiori is a more nuanced decision: some managers sell because his availability for Gameweek 10 is uncertain and they want Arsenal defensive cover then, but most hold for now in case he is fit for Gameweek 9 or clearer news emerges. Cherki, King, Wissa and Gonzalo are among other commonly sold players, while experts generally resist the wider-market urge to sell Cole Palmer; every expert owner keeps him.

Captaincy is close to unanimous. Erling Haaland, owned by 99% of the expert group, receives 93% of captain votes for Brighton at home. Palmer away to Manchester United is the only meaningful alternative at 5%, helped by the fact that he has already served his suspension in the League Cup and is available for the Premier League fixture. Nicolas Jackson and Thiago receive isolated differential captaincy support, but Haaland remains the safe and overwhelmingly recommended choice.
key_points: Sell João Pedro if possible: he is expected to miss at least Gameweeks 9 and 10, and 80% of expert owners transfer him out.
Nicolas Jackson is the priority forward buy, especially for João Pedro, Gonzalo or Wissa owners, due to Aston Villa's long favourable fixture run and Fulham at home in Gameweek 9.
Use Isak or Evanilson mainly as second-forward replacements rather than ahead of Jackson; Isak's Arsenal fixture reduces his immediate appeal.
Tavernier is the leading midfield transfer for Leeds at home, with Saka, Sangaré and Cherki viable routes out.
Silva is the preferred defensive buy, while Calafiori owners largely wait for further fitness news rather than selling immediately.
Captain Haaland against Brighton at home; Palmer is the main differential alternative against Manchester United.
Gameweek 9 is not viewed as a week to roll: 92% of experts make at least one transfer or use a chip, with about 7% on a Wildcard or Free Hit.

items.title: FPL GW9 WILDCARD DRAFT! 📝 GABRIEL IN? 🇧🇷 🔴 TEMPLATE WILDCARD TEAM SELECTION #fpl #premierleague
items.headline: Haaland captains a budget-heavy Gameweek 9 Wildcard as premium midfielders are ignored
items.summary:
A Gameweek 9 Wildcard is built around Erling Haaland as the only essential premium, with the Manchester City striker handed the captaincy almost every week because no high-priced midfielder is producing consistently enough to justify the investment. Nicolas Jackson takes the vice-captaincy, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin completes the forward line; Evan Ferguson is presented as a viable alternative in that third-striker slot.

David Raya remains the preferred goalkeeper despite Arsenal travelling to Liverpool in Gameweek 9. The defence prioritises low-cost starters, with Antonio Silva, Chris Mepham and Jan Paul van Hecke included to free funds for an Arsenal double-up featuring Gabriel. Ezri Konsa is a more uncertain pick because of the possible return of William Saliba, while Calafiori is flagged, and Jarrad Branthwaite is also part of the defensive options.

The midfield deliberately avoids Bruno Fernandes, Bukayo Saka and Cole Palmer. Morgan Rogers is the most expensive midfielder selected, valued as a well-priced route into Chelsea's attack when the side clicks. Pascal Gross keeps his place despite facing Manchester City in Gameweek 9 after coming close to an attacking return against Liverpool in Gameweek 8, while Marcus Tavernier and Manzambi provide cheaper midfield cover.

Cody Gakpo is retained as a bench option even though he faces Gabriel this week, with Liverpool's fixtures improving significantly from Gameweek 10 onwards. The central Wildcard trade-off is accepting budget and rotation risks in defence and midfield in exchange for Haaland, Jackson and a stronger forward-heavy structure, rather than spreading funds across several premium midfielders.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the standout captain for Gameweek 9 and is expected to keep the armband most weeks in this Wildcard structure.
Nicolas Jackson is vice-captain, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin selected up front and Evan Ferguson offered as an alternative.
David Raya is retained despite Arsenal's away fixture against Liverpool in Gameweek 9.
Gabriel provides an Arsenal defensive double-up, while Antonio Silva, Chris Mepham and Jan Paul van Hecke are budget defensive enablers.
The midfield excludes Bruno Fernandes, Bukayo Saka and Cole Palmer, with Morgan Rogers the most expensive midfielder selected.
Pascal Gross remains despite Manchester City in Gameweek 9 after nearly returning against Liverpool in Gameweek 8.
Cody Gakpo is held for Liverpool's stronger fixture run from Gameweek 10, even though he faces Arsenal this week.
Konsa carries uncertainty around Saliba's return, while Calafiori is yellow-flagged.
